question: How much does access to an environment model (full game source with permitted self-simulation) contribute to a bounded model editor's ability to improve the Seaquest Gold policy by direct weight edits, versus prose rules only?
editor: claude-opus-5-5 via Claude Code general-purpose subagents, 6 in parallel, no communication; budgets as v2
budget: <= 1.2M subagent tokens total; 6 dev passes x <= 1000 episodes, 25 sandbox runs, ~60 min per session
primary_endpoint: per-session held-out paired difference vs Gold (2,000 fresh episodes, active controls); success = 95% CI above 0 and above the best control
secondary: number of successful sessions per condition (S vs N); with n=3 per condition this is descriptive, not a powered test
joint comparison of all distinct submitted patches on 4,000 shared fresh seeds with Holm correction
dev-vs-held-out agreement; distinct candidates per condition (convergence); rule compliance (self-reported and from session logs)
operator_actions_before_launch: operator called `brief --game-source` once in sessions v3S-e1 and v3N-e1 to verify the condition-specific context (logged in those session logs)
prose_context_derivation: work/derived/editor-context/seaquest_rules_prose.txt = seaquest_game_source.txt up to the line starting 'The game's exact implementation' + the 'THE INPUT' section up to (excluding) 'How the 6 channels are built' (reproduce.md)
